files.notes/close_checklist.md:
# June 2026 close — controller's checklist

Prepared by F. Boudreau. Complete in sequence; clear each item before moving on.

1. Reconcile operating cash to the June bank statement. For every book-side item identified by the reconciliation, prepare one correcting journal entry per item.
2. Review the payroll register for any pay period ending after 6/30 that pays in July. If one exists, accrue the full gross wages to Accrued Liabilities; note that in some months every payroll run pays in-month.
3. Confirm June prepaid amortization against the prepaid schedule and underlying contracts. Check the GL first to prevent duplication. If the amortization is missing, book June as ONE combined journal entry. Apply the convention that a full month is taken in the month each prepaid item begins.
4. Book June depreciation per the fixed asset register, after verifying the GL to ensure it has not already been recorded.
5. Compare the June vendor-bill documents with the GL expense coding. Verify that each bill is charged to the correct expense account and reclass anything miscoded.
6. Prepare June budget-vs-actual variance commentary on an as-closed basis, only after items 1-5 have been booked.
files.notes/company_background.md:
# Company background

Foundry Line Industries began in 1998, when a toolmaker and a production supervisor set up a modest job shop to serve regional equipment builders that needed dependable short-run parts without a long procurement cycle. The business grew through repeat work, practical engineering support, and a reputation for calling customers early when a drawing or tolerance looked likely to cause trouble on the floor.

Today, Foundry Line Industries manufactures machined brackets, housings, guards, fittings, and other made-to-order metal components. Its customers span industrial equipment, marine, laboratory, and specialty-product markets. Work typically moves from drawing review and material planning through machining, fabrication, finishing, inspection, and shipment.

The team has the familiar character of a small manufacturer: experienced operators who know the machines by sound, newer technicians cross-training across cells, a purchasing lead who keeps close tabs on lead times, and office staff who handle customer schedules with a direct, no-fuss style. Production and accounting work closely because job timing, material receipts, and vendor paperwork often cross month-end.

The company is currently focused on keeping delivery performance steady, tightening documentation, and broadening relationships with repeat customers. Management is also refreshing its market presence while preserving the responsive service and shop-floor judgment that built the business.
files.notes/marketing_plan_h2.md:
# H2 marketing plan — working draft

## Direction

Position Foundry Line Industries as the practical manufacturing partner for buyers who value responsive quoting, clear production communication, and dependable short-run component work.

## Priorities

- Refresh core messaging around machining, fabrication, finishing, inspection, and schedule visibility.
- Build customer-facing examples that show how the team resolves drawing, tolerance, and manufacturability questions before they disrupt production.
- Host two educational webinars per quarter for engineers and purchasing teams.
- Pilot partner co-marketing with a complementary finishing, materials, or equipment business.
- Improve follow-up with past customers and dormant accounts using concise, industry-specific outreach.

## Content themes

- Practical design-for-manufacture guidance
- Shop-floor quality checks
- Material and lead-time planning
- Short-run and repeat-order coordination
- Employee craft and cross-training

## Quarter focus

### Q3

Finalize the brand refresh, update service-page copy, collect shop photography, and prepare the first webinar series. Select a co-marketing partner and agree on shared topics and review responsibilities.

### Q4

Publish customer-use stories, continue the webinar cadence, evaluate partner-pilot engagement, and refine outreach by market segment. Capture sales-team feedback on lead quality and recurring customer questions.

## Measures

Track qualified inquiries, webinar attendance, follow-up conversations, returning-account engagement, and sales feedback. Budget remains pending completion of the Q2 close.

# Handoff memo

F. Boudreau — a few things from my side before you finish the close:

- The bank usually posts its own fees and service charges near the end of the statement. We have historically recorded those during close rather than during the month, so check the final statement activity carefully.
- I moved quickly through June, and the expense coding on one or two vendor bills may be wrong. Treat the supporting documents in `bills/` as authoritative and reclass the GL where needed.
- The budget was fixed early in the quarter. The one-off June items were never planned, and they are generally the reason the larger budget variances appear.
- This month, the June 16-30 payroll run pays in the first days of July, not in June. The payroll register has the timing detail.
